documents.title: Testament
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: Dictated by Francis in the last months of his life, this is his most personal text: he rereads his conversion and entrusts the brothers with his spiritual will. It is not a juridical rule but a testimony.
documents.manuscriptNote: A broad manuscript tradition; the critical text is found in editions of the Opuscula (for example, K. Esser's edition).
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain (Wikisource transcription, 11 Nov 2026). English rendering: an editorial translation original to this app.

documents.title: Canticle of the Creatures (Canticle of Brother Sun)
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: A hymn composed by Francis in the final season of his life, perhaps in two stages (the stanza on forgiveness and the stanza on death may have been added later). It is considered the first poetic text of Italian literature.
documents.manuscriptNote: An early witness: Codex 338 of the Sacred Convent of Assisi (ff. 33r–34r).
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain (Wikisource transcription, 11 Nov 2026). English rendering: an editorial translation original to this app.

documents.title: The Later Rule (Regula bullata)
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: The definitive rule of the fraternity, approved by the bull of Honorius III on 29 November 1223. A brief text, still the foundation of the Order of Friars Minor.
documents.manuscriptNote: A broad manuscript tradition; the critical text is found in editions of the Opuscula.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain (Wikisource transcription, 11 Nov 2026). English rendering: an editorial translation original to this app.

documents.title: The Earlier Rule (Regula non bullata)
documents.author: Francis of Assisi and his first companions
documents.description: The fraternity's first complete rule, longer and more spiritual than the Later Rule, never formally approved by the Church. It preserves the freer voice of early Franciscan life.
documents.manuscriptNote: Preserved in only a few manuscripts; rediscovered by modern scholarship.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain (Wikisource transcription, 11 Nov 2026). English rendering: an editorial translation original to this app.

documents.title: Admonitions
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: Twenty-eight brief spiritual instructions for the fraternity: humility, obedience, patience, purity of heart. They are among the densest texts of Franciscan teaching.
documents.manuscriptNote: A complex manuscript tradition; the numbering follows the critical editions.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: Letter to a Minister
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: A letter to a guardian (minister) of the fraternity: how to receive brothers who fall, without harshness and without taking scandal.
documents.manuscriptNote: Transmitted in the tradition of the Opuscula.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: Letter to Brother Leo
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: A brief autograph letter to Brother Leo, his confessor and companion, about listening to one's conscience before God. It is precious also because it is an autograph document.
documents.manuscriptNote: Autograph preserved at the cathedral of Spoleto.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: Letter to the Entire Order
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: A letter to the brothers, largely about the Eucharist, reverence for God's written words, and observance of the Rule. It is one of Francis's longer writings.
documents.manuscriptNote: Transmitted in the Opuscula tradition. Text from the Latin Wikisource transcription.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval Latin original: public domain. Translation: original to this app.

documents.title: Praises of God Most High
documents.author: Francis of Assisi
documents.description: A prayer of praise composed at La Verna, transmitted on the same autograph sheet as the Letter to Brother Leo and the blessing for him.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: The First Life of Thomas of Celano
documents.author: Thomas of Celano
documents.description: The first official biography of Francis, commissioned by Gregory IX for the canonization. It is the principal source closest to the saint, although written with hagiographic aims.
documents.manuscriptNote: Modern critical editions are available; numbering is by paragraph.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: The Second Life of Thomas of Celano
documents.author: Thomas of Celano
documents.description: The second biography, gathering the testimonies of companions still living: richer in episodes and in details of Francis's character.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: Bonaventure's Major Life
documents.author: Bonaventure of Bagnoregio
documents.description: A theological biography of Francis written by Bonaventure, which became the Order's official life in 1266. It is more constructed and doctrinal than Celano's lives.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: The Little Flowers of Saint Francis
documents.author: Anonymous Franciscan (from a Latin tradition, the Actus)
documents.description: A vernacular collection of episodes about Francis and his companions, translated and reworked from fourteenth-century Latin texts (the Actus beati Francisci). A literary masterpiece: its tales bear witness to devotion, not to historically verifiable chronicle.
documents.manuscriptNote: Italian version of the Actus; numerous manuscripts and printed editions.
documents.licenseNote: Medieval original: public domain. English paraphrase: original editorial text for this app.

documents.title: The So-called "Simple Prayer"
documents.author: Anonymous modern author (first known publication: 1912, French journal La Clochette)
documents.description: The prayer "Make me an instrument of your peace" is beloved and spiritually close to Franciscan sensibility, but it is NOT by Francis: it first appeared in 1912 and was attributed to him only later. We include it for historical honesty: the app will never use it as a saying of the saint.
documents.manuscriptNote: No medieval attestation. See studies by P. Patrice Mahieu and surveys on sanfrancesco.org.
documents.licenseNote: Modern text: not reproduced in full in this app.

documents.title: Original Game Narrative
documents.author: App editorial team
documents.description: A documentary placeholder for the Wayfarer chapters and card scenarios: original historical fiction, inspired by the sources but never presented as historical fact or as Francis's own words.

passages.originalText: Dominus ita dedit mihi fratri Francisco incipere faciendi poenitentiam: quia, cum essem in peccatis, nimis mihi videbatur amarum videre leprosos. Et ipse Dominus conduxit me inter illos et feci misericordiam cum illis. Et recedente me ab ipsis, id quod videbatur mihi amarum, conversum fuit mihi in dulcedinem animi et corporis; et postea parum steti et exivi de saeculo.
passages.translation: The Lord Himself granted me, Brother Francis, to begin to do penance in this way: when I was in sin, it seemed too bitter for me to see lepers. And the Lord Himself led me among them, and I showed them mercy. And when I had left them, what had seemed bitter was changed for me into sweetness of soul and body; and afterwards I lingered but a little while and went forth from the world.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Et Dominus dedit mihi talem fidem in ecclesiis, ut ita simpliciter orarem et dicerem Adoramus te, Domine Jesu Christe et ad omnes ecclesias tuas, quae sunt in toto mundo, et benedicimus tibi, quia per sanctam crucem tuam redimisti mundum. Postea Dominus dedit mihi et dat tantam fidem in sacerdotibus, qui vivunt secundum formam sanctae ecclesiae Romanae propter ordinem ipsorum, quod si facerent mihi persecutionem, volo recurrere ad ipsos. Et si haberem tantam sapientiam, quantam Salomon habuit, et invenirem pauperculos sacerdotes huius saeculi, in parochiis, quibus morantur, nolo praedicare ultra voluntatem ipsorum. Et ipsos et omnes alios volo timere, amare et honorare sicut meos dominos. Et nolo in ipsis considerare peccatum, quia Filium Dei discerno in ipsis, et domini mei sunt. Et propter hoc facio, quia nihil video corporaliter in hoc saeculo de ipso altissimo Filio Dei, nisi sanctissimum corpus et sanctissimum sanguinem suum, quod ipsi recipiunt et ipsi soli aliis ministrant. Et haec sanctissima mysteria super omnia volo honorari, venerari et in locis pretiosis collocari. Sanctissima nomina et verba eius scripta, ubicumque invenero in locis illicitis, volo colligere et rogo, quod colligantur et in loco honesto collocentur. Et omnes theologos et qui ministrant sanctissima verba divina, debemus honorare et venerari, sicut qui ministrant nobis spiritum et vitam (cfr. Joa 6,64).
passages.translation: And the Lord gave me such faith in churches that I would pray and say simply: We adore you, Lord Jesus Christ, in all your churches throughout the whole world, and we bless you, because by your holy cross you have redeemed the world. Afterwards the Lord gave me, and still gives me, such faith in the priests who live according to the form of the holy Roman Church, on account of their order, that even if they persecuted me I would want to turn to them. And if I had as much wisdom as Solomon had, and I found poor little priests of this world in the parishes where they live, I do not want to preach against their will. Them, and all others, I want to fear, love and honour as my lords. And I do not want to consider sin in them, because I discern the Son of God in them, and they are my lords. I do this because, of the most high Son of God himself, I see nothing in this world with my bodily eyes except his most holy body and most holy blood, which they receive and they alone minister to others. And these most holy mysteries I want honoured above all things, venerated, and placed in precious places. His most holy names and his written words, wherever I find them in unfit places, I want gathered up, and I ask that they be gathered and placed in a fitting place. And all theologians, and those who minister the most holy divine words, we must honour and venerate, as those who minister spirit and life to us.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Et postquam Dominus dedit mihi de fratribus, nemo ostendebat mihi, quid deberem facere, sed ipse Altissimus revelavit mihi, quod deberem vivere secundum formam sancti Evangelii. Et ego paucis verbis et simpliciter feci scribi et dominus papa confirmavit mihi. Et illi qui veniebant ad recipiendam vitam, omnia quae habere poterant (Tob 1,3), dabant pauperibus; et erant contenti tunica una, intus et foris repeciata, cum cingulo et braccis. Et nolebamus plus habere. Officium dicebamus clerici secundum alios clericos, laici dicebant Pater noster; et satis libenter manebamus in ecclesiis. Et eramus idiotae et subditi omnibus. Et ego manibus meis laborabam, et volo laborare; et omnes alii fratres firmiter volo, quod laborent de laboritio, quod pertinet ad honestatem. Qui nesciunt, discant, non propter cupiditatem recipiendi pretium laboris, sed propter exemplum et ad repellendam otiositatem. Et quando non daretur nobis pretium laboris, recurramus ad mensam Domini, petendo eleemosynam ostiatim.
passages.translation: And after the Lord gave me brothers, no one showed me what I ought to do, but the Most High himself revealed to me that I should live according to the form of the holy Gospel. And I had it written down in few words and simply, and the lord pope confirmed it for me. And those who came to take up this life gave to the poor everything they could have, and were content with one tunic, patched inside and out, with the cord and the trousers. And we did not want to have more. We who were clerics said the office as other clerics do; the lay brothers said the Our Father; and we stayed in churches gladly enough. And we were unlettered and subject to everyone. And I worked with my hands, and I want to work; and I firmly want all the other brothers to work at labour that belongs to honesty. Those who do not know how should learn, not out of greed for the wage of the work, but for the sake of example and to drive off idleness. And when the wage of the work is not given us, let us turn to the Lord's table, asking alms from door to door.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Salutationem mihi Dominus revelavit, ut diceremus Dominus det tibi pacem.
passages.translation: The Lord revealed a greeting to me, that we should say: The Lord give you peace.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Caveant sibi fratres, ut ecclesias, habitacula paupercula et omnia, quae pro ipsis construuntur, penitus non recipiant, nisi essent, sicut decet sanctam paupertatem, quam in regula promisimus, semper ibi hospitantes sicut advenae et peregrini (cfr. 1 Petr 2,11). Praecipio firmiter per obedientiam fratribus universis, quod ubicumque sunt, non audeant petere aliquam litteram in curia Romana per se neque per interpositam personam, neque pro ecclesia neque pro alio loco neque sub specie praedicationis neque pro persecutione suorum corporum; sed ubicumque non fuerint recepti, fugiant in aliam terram ad faciendam poenitentiam cum benedictione Dei.
passages.translation: Let the brothers beware of receiving churches, poor little dwellings, and everything built for them, unless these be as befits the holy poverty we promised in the Rule, always staying there as strangers and pilgrims. I firmly command all the brothers by obedience that, wherever they are, they not dare to seek any letter from the Roman curia, either by themselves or through another person, neither for a church nor for any other place, nor under the appearance of preaching, nor because of persecution of their bodies; but wherever they have not been received, let them flee to another land to do penance with the blessing of God.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Et firmiter volo obedire ministro generali huius fraternitatis et alio guardiano, quem sibi placuerit mihi dare. Et ita volo esse captus in manibus suis, ut non possim ire vel facere ultra obedientiam et voluntatem suam, quia dominus meus est. Et quamvis sim simplex et infirmus, tamen semper volo habere clericum, qui mihi faciat officium, sicut in regula continetur. Et omnes alii fratres teneantur ita obedire guardianis suis et facere officium secundum regulam. Et qui inventi essent, quod non facerent officium secundum regulam, et vellent alio modo variare, aut non essent catholici, omnes fratres, ubicumque sunt, per obedientiam teneantur, quod ubicumque invenerint aliquem ipsorum, proximiori custodi illius loci, ubi ipsum invenerint, debeant repraesentare. Et custos firmiter teneatur per obedientiam ipsum fortiter custodire, sicuti hominem in vinculis die noctuque, ita quod non possit eripi de manibus suis, donec propria sua persona ipsum repraesentet in manibus sui ministri. Et minister firmiter teneatur per obedientiam mittendi ipsum per tales fratres, quod die noctuque custodiant ipsum sicuti hominem in vinculis, donec repraesentent ipsum coram domino Ostiensi, qui est dominus, protector et corrector totius fraternitatis. Et non dicant fratres Haec est alia regula; quia haec est recordatio, admonitio, exhortatio et meum testamentum, quod ego frater Franciscus parvulus facio vobis fratribus meis benedictis propter hoc, ut regulam, quam Domino promisimus, melius catholice observemus.
passages.translation: And I firmly want to obey the minister general of this fraternity and the guardian it pleases him to give me. And I want to be so held in his hands that I cannot go or act beyond obedience and his will, because he is my lord. And although I am simple and ill, I still always want to have a cleric who says the office for me, as is contained in the Rule. And all the other brothers are bound to obey their guardians in the same way and to say the office according to the Rule. And if any were found who did not say the office according to the Rule and wanted to change it in some other way, or were not Catholic, all the brothers, wherever they are, are bound by obedience, wherever they find one of them, to present him to the custodian nearest the place where they found him. And the custodian is firmly bound by obedience to guard him closely, like a man in chains, day and night, so that he cannot be taken from his hands, until he himself presents him into the hands of his minister. And the minister is firmly bound by obedience to send him by such brothers as will guard him day and night like a man in chains, until they present him before the lord of Ostia, who is lord, protector and corrector of the whole fraternity. And let the brothers not say: This is another rule. For this is a remembrance, an admonition, an exhortation, and my testament, which I, Brother Francis, the little one, make for you, my blessed brothers, so that we may observe in a more Catholic way the Rule we promised the Lord.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Et generalis minister et omnes alii ministri et custodes per obedientiam teneantur, in istis verbis non addere vel minuere. Et semper hoc scriptum habeant secum iuxta regulam. Et in omnibus capitulis, quae faciunt, quando legunt regulam, legant et ista verba. Et omnibus fratribus meis clericis et laicis praecipio firmiter per obedientiam, ut non mittant glossas in regula neque in istis verbis dicendo Ita volunt intelligi. Sed sicut dedit mihi Dominus simpliciter et pure dicere et scribere regulam et ista verba, ita simpliciter et sine glossa intelligatis et cum sancta operatione observetis usque in finem. Et quicumque haec observaverit, in caelo repleatur benedictione altissimi Patris et in terra repleatur benedictione dilecti Filii sui cum sanctissimo Spiritu Paraclito et omnibus virtutibus caelorum et omnibus sanctis. Et ego frater Franciscus parvulus, vester servus, quantumcumque possum, confirmo vobis intus et foris istam sanctissimam benedictionem. en The Testament of St. Francis of Assisi hr Oporuka svetoga Franje ru Завещание (Франциск Ассизский)
passages.translation: And the minister general and all the other ministers and custodians are bound by obedience not to add to these words or take anything away. And let them always have this writing with them, beside the Rule. And in all the chapters they hold, when they read the Rule, let them read these words as well. And I firmly command all my brothers, clerics and lay, by obedience, not to place glosses on the Rule or on these words, saying: They are to be understood thus. But as the Lord gave me to say and write the Rule and these words simply and purely, so understand them simply and without a gloss, and observe them with holy work until the end. And whoever has observed these things, may he be filled in heaven with the blessing of the most high Father, and on earth with the blessing of his beloved Son, with the most holy Spirit, the Paraclete, and with all the virtues of heaven and all the saints. And I, Brother Francis, the little one, your servant, as much as I can, confirm for you, within and without, this most holy blessing.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: Altissimu, onnipotente, bon Signore, tue so' le laude, la gloria e l'honore et onne benedictione. Ad te solo, Altissimo, se konfano, et nullu homo ène dignu te mentovare. Laudato sie, mi' Signore, cum tucte le tue creature, spetialmente messor lo frate sole, lo qual' è iorno, et allumini noi per lui.
passages.translation: Most High, all-powerful, good Lord, yours are the praises, the glory, the honour, and every blessing. To you alone, Most High, do they belong, and no human is worthy to speak your name. Praised be you, my Lord, with all your creatures, especially Sir Brother Sun, who is the day, and through whom you give us light.
passages.note: Umbrian of Assisi codex 338, in the reading already used for vv. 1-9. The rest was compared with the diplomatic transcription on Italian Wikisource, Cantico di Frate Sole (11 Nov 2026); concordant forms were restored where the scan breaks a word. Editorial translation original to this app.

passages.reference: Canticle of the Creatures, middle stanzas
passages.originalText: Et ellu è bellu e radiante cum grande splendore: de te, Altissimo, porta significatione. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per sora luna e le stelle: in celu l'ài formate clarite et pretiose et belle. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per frate vento et per aere et nubilo et sereno et onne tempo, per lo quale a le tue creature dài sustentamento. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per sor'acqua, la quale è multo utile et humile et pretiosa et casta. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per frate focu, per lo quale ennallumini la nocte: et ello è bello et iocundo et robustoso et forte. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per sora nostra matre terra, la quale ne sustenta et governa, et produce diversi fructi con coloriti flori et herba.
passages.translation: And he is beautiful and radiant, with great splendour: of you, Most High, he bears the meaning. Praised be you, my Lord, through Sister Moon and the stars: in heaven you formed them, clear and precious and beautiful. Praised be you, my Lord, through Brother Wind, and through air and cloud and fair weather and every weather, through which you give sustenance to your creatures. Praised be you, my Lord, through Sister Water, who is very useful and humble and precious and chaste. Praised be you, my Lord, through Brother Fire, through whom you light up the night: and he is beautiful and joyful and robust and strong. Praised be you, my Lord, through our Sister Mother Earth, who sustains and governs us, and produces varied fruits with coloured flowers and grass.
passages.note: Umbrian of Assisi codex 338, in the reading already used for vv. 1-9. The rest was compared with the diplomatic transcription on Italian Wikisource, Cantico di Frate Sole (11 Nov 2026); concordant forms were restored where the scan breaks a word. Editorial translation original to this app.

passages.reference: Canticle of the Creatures, final stanzas
passages.originalText: Laudato si', mi' Signore, per quelli ke perdonano per lo tuo amore et sostengono infirmitate et tribulatione. Beati quelli ke 'l sosterranno in pace, ka da te, Altissimo, sirano incoronati. Laudato si', mi' Signore, per sora nostra morte corporale, da la quale nullu homo vivente pò skappare: guai a quelli ke morrano ne le peccata mortali; beati quelli ke trovarà ne le tue sanctissime voluntati, ka la morte secunda no 'l farrà male. Laudate et benedicete mi' Signore et rengratiate e serviateli cum grande humilitate.
passages.translation: Praised be you, my Lord, through those who forgive for your love and bear illness and tribulation. Blessed are those who endure them in peace, for by you, Most High, they shall be crowned. Praised be you, my Lord, through our Sister Bodily Death, from whom no living person can escape: woe to those who die in mortal sin; blessed are those whom she finds in your most holy will, for the second death shall do them no harm. Praise and bless my Lord, and give thanks, and serve him with great humility.
passages.note: Umbrian of Assisi codex 338, in the reading already used for vv. 1-9. The rest was compared with the diplomatic transcription on Italian Wikisource, Cantico di Frate Sole (11 Nov 2026); concordant forms were restored where the scan breaks a word. Editorial translation original to this app.

passages.reference: Bull of Honorius III, preface to the Rule
passages.originalText: Honorius episcopus servus servorum dei dilectis filiis, fratri Francisco et aliis fratribus de ordine fratrum minorum, salutem et apostolicam benedictionem. Solet annuere sedes apostolica piis votis et honestis petentium desideriis favorem benivolum impertiri. Eapropter, dilecti in domino filii, vestris piis precibus inclinati, ordinis vestri regulam, a bone memorie Innocentio papa, predecessore nostro, approbatam, annotatam presentibus, auctoritate vobis apostolica confirmamus et presentis scripti patrocinio communimus, que talis est Regula minorum fratrum.
passages.translation: Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Brother Francis and the other brothers of the Order of Minors: greeting and apostolic blessing. The apostolic see is accustomed to grant the pious vows and honest desires of those who ask, and to impart a kindly favour. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your pious prayers, we confirm for you by apostolic authority the rule of your Order, approved by Pope Innocent of good memory, our predecessor, and copied here, and we strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. It is this: the Rule of the Lesser Brothers.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Regula et Vita Minorum Fratrum haec est, scilicet Domini nostri Jesu Christi sanctum Evangelium observare vivendo in obedientia, sine proprio et in castitate. [2] Frater Franciscus promittit obedientiam et reverentiam domino papae Honorio ac successoribus eius canonice intrantibus et Ecclesiae Romanae. [3] Et alii fratres teneantur fratri Francisco et eius successoribus obedire.
passages.translation: The Rule and life of the Lesser Brothers is this: to observe the holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, living in obedience, without anything of one's own, and in chastity. Brother Francis promises obedience and reverence to the lord pope Honorius and his canonically elected successors, and to the Roman Church. And the other brothers are bound to obey Brother Francis and his successors.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Si qui voluerint hanc vitam accipere et venerint ad fratres nostros, mittant eos ad suos ministros provinciales, quibus solummodo et non aliis recipiendi fratres licentia concedatur. [2] Ministri vero diligenter examinent eos de fide catholica et ecclesiasticis sacramentis. [3] Et si haec omnia credant et velint ea fideliter confiteri et usque in finem firmiter observare [4] et uxores non habent vel, si habent, et iam monasterium intraverint uxores vel licentiam eis dederint auctoritate diocesani episcopi, voto continentiae iam emisso, et illius sint aetatis uxores, quod non possit de eis oriri suspicio, [5] dicant illis verbum sancti Evangelii (cfr. Mt 19,21 par), quod vadant et vendant omnia sua et ea studeant pauperibus erogare. [6] Quod si facere non potuerint, sufficit eis bona voluntas. [7] Et caveant fratres et eorum ministri, ne solliciti sint de rebus suis temporalibus, ut libere faciant de rebus suis, quidquid Dominus inspiraverit eis. [8] Si tamen consilium requiratur, licentiam habeant ministri mittendi eos ad aliquos Deum timentes, quorum consilio bona sua pauperibus erogentur. [9] Postea concedant eis pannos probationis, videlicet duas tunicas sine caputio et cingulum et braccas et caparonem usque ad cingulum, [10] nisi eisdem ministris aliud secundum Deum aliquando videatur. [11] Finito vero anno probationis, recipiantur ad obedientiam promittentes vitam istam semper et regulam observare. [12] Et nullo modo licebit eis de ista religione exire iuxta mandatum domini papae, [13] quia secundum sanctum Evangelium nemo mittens manum ad aratrum et aspiciens retro aptus est regno Dei (Lc 9,62). [14] Et illi qui iam promiserunt obedientiam habeant unam tunicam cum caputio et aliam sine caputio qui voluerint habere. [15] Et qui necessitate coguntur possint portare calciamenta. [16] Et fratres omnes vestimentis vilibus induantur et possint ea repeciare de saccis et aliis peciis cum benedictione Dei. [17] Quos moneo et exhortor, ne despiciant neque iudicent homines, quos vident mollibus vestimentis et coloratis indutos, uti cibis et potibus delicatis, sed magis unusquisque iudicet et despiciat semetipsum.
passages.translation: If any wish to take up this life and come to our brothers, let them be sent to their provincial ministers, to whom alone permission to receive brothers is granted. The ministers are to examine them carefully on the Catholic faith and the sacraments of the Church. If they believe all this and mean to confess it faithfully and keep it firmly to the end, and they have no wives, or if they do and the wives have already entered a monastery or, by authority of the diocesan bishop and with a vow of continence already made, have given permission, and are of such an age that no suspicion can arise, let the brothers tell them the word of the holy Gospel: that they go, sell all that is theirs, and take care to give it to the poor. If they cannot, good will is enough. Let the brothers and their ministers beware of concerning themselves with those temporal goods, so that the newcomers may dispose of them freely as the Lord inspires. If counsel is sought, the ministers may send them to people who fear God, by whose advice the goods are given to the poor. Then let them give the clothes of probation: two tunics without a hood, the cord, trousers, and a cape to the cord, unless the ministers sometimes judge otherwise according to God. When the year of probation ends, let them be received into obedience, promising always to observe this life and the Rule. It will not be lawful for them to leave, according to the pope's command, because no one who puts a hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God. Those who have already promised obedience are to have one tunic with a hood and, if they wish, another without. Those forced by necessity may wear shoes. Let all the brothers wear poor clothes, and they may patch them with sackcloth and other pieces, with God's blessing. I admonish and exhort them not to despise or judge people dressed in soft and coloured clothes, who use delicate food and drink: let each instead judge and despise himself.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Clerici faciant divinum officium secundum ordinem sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae excepto psalterio, [2] ex quo habere poterunt breviaria. [3] Laici vero dicant viginti quattuor Pater noster pro matutino, pro laude quinque, pro prima, tertia, sexta, nona, pro qualibet istarum septem, pro vesperis autem duodecim, pro completorio septem; [4] et orent pro defunctis. [5] Et ieiunent a festo Omnium Sanctorum usque ad Nativitatem Domini. [6] Sanctam vero quadragesimam, quae incipit ab Epiphania usque ad continuos quadraginta dies, quam Dominus suo sancto ieiunio consecravit (cfr. Mt 4,2), qui voluntarie eam ieiunant benedicti sint a Domino, et qui nolunt non sint astricti. [7] Sed aliam usque ad Resurrectionem Domini ieiunent. [8] Aliis autem temporibus non teneantur nisi sexta feria ieiunare. [9] Tempore vero manifestae necessitatis non teneantur fratres ieiunio corporali. [10] Consulo vero, moneo et exhortor fratres meos in Domino Jesu Christo, ut, quando vadunt per mundum, non litigent neque contendant verbis (cfr. 2 Tim 2,14), nec alios iudicent; [11] sed sint mites, pacifici et modesti, mansueti et humiles, honeste loquentes omnibus, sicut decet. [12] Et non debeant equitare, nisi manifesta necessitate vel infirmitate cogantur. [13] In quamcumque domum intraverint, primum dicant Pax huic domui (cfr. Lc 10,5). [14] Et secundum sanctum Evangelium de omnibus cibis, qui apponuntur eis, liceat manducare (cfr. Lc 10,8).
passages.translation: Let the clerics say the divine office according to the rite of the holy Roman Church, except the psalter, for which they may have breviaries. Let the lay brothers say twenty-four Our Fathers for matins, five for lauds, seven each for prime, terce, sext and none, twelve for vespers and seven for compline, and let them pray for the dead. Let them fast from All Saints until Christmas. The Lent that begins at Epiphany and lasts forty days, which the Lord consecrated by his own fast, those who fast it freely are blessed by the Lord, and those who do not wish to are not bound. The other Lent, until the Resurrection, let them fast. At other times they are bound to fast only on Friday. In manifest necessity they are not bound to a fast of the body. I counsel, admonish and exhort my brothers in the Lord Jesus Christ: when they go through the world, let them not quarrel, contend in words, or judge others; let them be meek, peaceful, modest, gentle and humble, and speak honestly to everyone, as is fitting. Let them not ride unless forced by manifest necessity or illness. Into whatever house they enter, let them first say: Peace to this house. And according to the Gospel they may eat any food set before them.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Praecipio firmiter fratribus universis, ut nullo modo denarios vel pecuniam recipiant per se vel per interpositam personam. [2] Tamen pro necessitatibus infirmorum et aliis fratribus induendis per amicos spirituales ministri tantum et custodes sollicitam curam gerant secundum loca et tempora et frigidas regiones, sicut necessitati viderint expedire; [3] eo semper salvo, ut, sicut dictum est, denarios vel pecuniam non recipiant.
passages.translation: I firmly command all the brothers not to receive coins or money in any way, by themselves or through another person. For the needs of the sick and for clothing the other brothers, only the ministers and custodians, through spiritual friends, are to take careful charge according to places, times and cold regions, as they see necessity requires; it remaining always the case that, as has been said, they do not receive coins or money.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Fratres illi, quibus gratiam dedit Dominus laborandi, laborent fideliter et devote, [2] ita quod, excluso otio animae inimico, sanctae orationis et devotionis spiritum non exstinguant, cui debent cetera temporalia deservire. [3] De mercede vero laboris pro se et suis fratribus corporis necessaria recipiant praeter denarios vel pecuniam [4] et hoc humiliter, sicut decet servos Dei et paupertatis sanctissimae sectatores.
passages.translation: Let the brothers to whom the Lord has given the grace of working work faithfully and devoutly, so that, with idleness the enemy of the soul shut out, they do not extinguish the spirit of holy prayer and devotion, which all other temporal things must serve. As the wage of work let them receive, for themselves and their brothers, what the body needs, except coins or money, and let them receive it humbly, as befits servants of God and followers of most holy poverty.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Fratres nihil sibi approprient nec domum nec locum nec aliquam rem. [2] Et tanquam peregrini et advenae (cfr. 1 Petr 2,11) in hoc saeculo in paupertate et humilitate Domino famulantes vadant pro eleemosyna confidenter, [3] nec oportet eos verecundari, quia Dominus pro nobis se fecit pauperem in hoc mundo (cfr. 2 Cor 8,9). [4] Haec est illa celsitudo altissimae paupertatis, quae vos, carissimos fratres meos, heredes et reges regni caelorum instituit, pauperes rebus fecit, virtutibus sublimavit (cfr. Jac 2,5). [5] Haec sit portio vestra, quae perducit in terram viventium (cfr. Ps 141,6). [6] Cui, dilectissimi fratres, totaliter inhaerentes nihil aliud pro nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi in perpetuum sub caelo habere velitis. [7] Et, ubicumque sunt et se invenerint fratres, ostendant se domesticos invicem inter se. [8] Et secure manifestet unus alteri necessitatem suam, quia, si mater nutrit et diligit filium suum (cfr. 1 Thess 2,7) carnalem, quanto diligentius debet quis diligere et nutrire fratrem suum spiritualem? [9] Et, si quis eorum in infirmitate ceciderit, alii fratres debent ei servire, sicut vellent sibi serviri (cfr. Mt 7,12).
passages.translation: Let the brothers appropriate nothing, neither house nor place nor anything. As pilgrims and strangers in this world, serving the Lord in poverty and humility, let them go for alms confidently, and they should not be ashamed, because the Lord made himself poor for us in this world. This is the summit of the highest poverty, which has made you, my dearest brothers, heirs and kings of the kingdom of heaven, poor in things and high in virtue. Let this be your portion, which leads into the land of the living. Clinging to it wholly, most beloved brothers, wish to have nothing else forever under heaven, for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Wherever the brothers are and meet, let them show themselves one household to each other. Let one make his need known to the other with confidence: if a mother feeds and loves her child according to the flesh, how much more must one love and feed his brother according to the spirit? And if one falls ill, let the other brothers serve him as they would wish to be served.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Si qui fratrum, instigante inimico, mortaliter peccaverint, pro illis peccatis, de quibus ordinatum fuerit inter fratres, ut recurratur ad solos ministros provinciales, teneantur praedicti fratres ad eos recurrere quam citius poterint, sine mora. [2] Ipsi vero ministri, si presbyteri sunt, cum misericordia iniungant illis poenitentiam; si vero presbyteri non sunt, iniungi faciant per alios sacerdotes ordinis, sicut eis secundum Deum melius videbitur expedire. [3] Et cavere debent, ne irascantur et conturbentur propter peccatum alicuius, quia ira et conturbatio in se et in aliis impediunt caritatem.
passages.translation: If some brothers, urged by the enemy, sin mortally, for those sins for which it is laid down among the brothers that recourse is to be had only to the provincial ministers, let them have recourse as soon as they can, without delay. The ministers, if they are priests, are to impose the penance with mercy; if they are not, let them have it imposed by other priests of the Order, as seems best according to God. Let them beware of anger and disturbance over anyone's sin: anger and disturbance block charity in oneself and in others.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Universi fratres unum de fratribus istius religionis teneantur semper habere generalem ministrum et servum totius fraternitatis et ei teneantur firmiter obedire. [2] Quo decedente, electio successoris fiat a ministris provincialibus et custodibus in capitulo Pentecostes, in quo provinciales ministri teneantur semper insimul convenire, ubicumque a generali ministro fuerit constitutum; [3] et hoc semel in tribus annis vel ad alium terminum maiorem vel minorem, sicut a praedicto ministro fuerit ordinatum. [4] Et si aliquo tempore appareret universitati ministrorum provincialium et custodum, praedictum ministrum non esse sufficientem ad servitium et communem utilitatem fratrum, teneantur praedicti fratres, quibus electio data est, in nomine Domini alium sibi eligere in custodem. [5] Post capitulum vero Pentecostes ministri et custodes possint singuli, si voluerint et eis expedire videbitur, eodem anno in suis custodiis semel fratres suos ad capitulum convocare.
passages.translation: Let all the brothers always have one brother of this religion as minister general and servant of the whole fraternity, and obey him firmly. At his death the successor is to be elected by the provincial ministers and custodians at the chapter of Pentecost, where the provincial ministers must always assemble, in the place set by the minister general, once every three years or at another term, longer or shorter, which he orders. If the body of ministers and custodians should find that minister insufficient for the service and common good of the brothers, those to whom the election belongs are bound, in the Lord's name, to elect another. After the Pentecost chapter, ministers and custodians may, if they wish and it seems useful, once in the same year call their own brothers to a chapter in their custody.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Fratres non praedicent in episcopatu alicuius episcopi, cum ab eo illis fuerit contradictum. [2] Et nullus fratrum populo penitus audeat praedicare, nisi a ministro generali huius fraternitatis fuerit examinatus et approbatus, et ab eo officium sibi praedicationis concessum. [3] Moneo quoque et exhortor eosdem fratres, ut in praedicatione, quam faciunt, sint examinata et casta eorum eloquia (cfr. Ps 11,7; 17,31), ad utilitatem et aedificationem populi, [4] annuntiando eis vitia et virtutes, poenam et gloriam cum brevitate sermonis; quia verbum abbreviatum fecit Dominus super terram (cfr. Rom 9,28).
passages.translation: Let the brothers not preach in a bishop's diocese when he has forbidden it. Let no brother dare preach to the people unless he has been examined and approved by the minister general, and unless the minister has granted him the office of preaching. I admonish and exhort the brothers: in preaching let their words be weighed and chaste, for the people's benefit and building up, announcing vices and virtues, punishment and glory, briefly, because the Lord made a shortened word upon the earth.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Fratres, qui sunt ministri et servi aliorum fratrum, visitent et moneant fratres suos et humiliter et caritative corrigant eos, non praecipientes eis aliquid, quod sit contra animam suam et regulam nostram. [2] Fratres vero, qui sunt subditi, recordentur, quod propter Deum abnegaverunt proprias voluntates. [3] Unde firmiter praecipio eis, ut obediant suis ministris in omnibus quae promiserunt Domino observare et non sunt contraria animae et regulae nostrae. [4] Et ubicumque sunt fratres, qui scirent et cognoscerent, se non posse regulam spiritualiter observare, ad suos ministros debeant et possint recurrere. [5] Ministri vero caritative et benigne eos recipiant et tantam familiaritatem habeant circa ipsos, ut dicere possint eis et facere sicut domini servis suis; [6] nam ita debet esse, quod ministri sint servi omnium fratrum. [7] Moneo vero et exhortor in Domino Jesu Christo, ut caveant fratres ab omni superbia, vana gloria, invidia, avaritia (cfr. Lc 12,15), cura et sollicitudine huius saeculi (cfr. Mt 13,22), detractione et murmuratione, et non curent nescientes litteras litteras discere; [8] sed attendant, quod super omnia desiderare debent habere Spiritum Domini et sanctam eius operationem, [9] orare semper ad eum puro corde et habere humilitatem, patientiam in persecutione et infirmitate [10] et diligere eos qui nos persequuntur et reprehendunt et arguunt, quia dicit Dominus Diligite inimicos vestros et orate pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos (cfr. Mt 5,44). [11] Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum (Mt 5,10). [12] Qui autem perseveraverit usque in finem hic salvus erit (Mt 10,22).
passages.translation: Brothers who are ministers and servants of the others are to visit and warn their brothers and correct them with humility and charity, commanding nothing against the soul and our Rule. Subject brothers are to remember that for God they have renounced their own wills. I firmly command them to obey their ministers in all they promised the Lord to observe that is not contrary to the soul and the Rule. Brothers who know they cannot observe the Rule spiritually ought and may turn to the ministers. Let the ministers receive them with charity and kindness, and be so familiar with them that they can speak and act as lords with their servants: for so it must be, that the ministers are servants of all the brothers. I admonish and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ: let the brothers beware of all pride, vainglory, envy and avarice, of the care and anxiety of this age, of slander and murmuring; and let one who does not know letters not be anxious to learn them. Let them attend rather to this: above all they should desire the Spirit of the Lord and his holy working, pray always with a pure heart, have humility and patience in persecution and illness, and love those who persecute, rebuke and accuse us, because the Lord says: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute and slander you. Blessed are those persecuted for justice, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Praecipio firmiter fratribus universis, ne habeant suspecta consortia vel consilia mulierum, [2] et ne ingrediantur monasteria monacharum praeter illos, quibus a sede apostolica concessa est licentia specialis; [3] nec fiant compatres virorum vel mulierum nec hac occasione inter fratres vel de fratribus scandalum oriatur.
passages.translation: I firmly command all the brothers not to keep suspicious company or counsel with women, and not to enter the monasteries of nuns except those to whom the apostolic see has given a special permission. They are not to become godfathers of men or women, lest scandal arise among the brothers or about them.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.reference: Later Rule, chapter XII and confirmation
passages.originalText: [1] Quicumque fratrum divina inspiratione voluerint ire inter saracenos et alios infideles petant inde licentiam a suis ministris provincialibus. [2] Ministri vero nullis eundi licentiam tribuant, nisi eis quos viderint esse idoneos ad mittendum. [3] Ad haec per obedientiam iniungo ministris, ut petant a domino papa unum de sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae cardinalibus, qui sit gubernator, protector et corrector istius fraternitatis, [4] ut semper subditi et subiecti pedibus eiusdem sanctae Ecclesiae stabiles in fide (cfr. Col 1,23) catholica paupertatem et humilitatem et sanctum evangelium Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quod firmiter promisimus, observemus. Explicit regula et vita fratrum minorum. Sequitur confirmatio regulae Nulli ergo omnino hominum liceat hanc paginam nostre confirmationis infringere, vel ei ausu temerario contraire. si quis autem hoc attentare presumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis dei et beatorum Petri et Pauli, apostolorum eius, se noverit incursurum. Datum Laterani tertio kalendas decembris, pontificatus nostri anno octavo. Honorius III hr Pravilo svetoga Franje
passages.translation: Any brother who by divine inspiration wishes to go among the Saracens and other unbelievers is to ask leave of his provincial minister. The ministers are to give it only to those they see fit to send. By obedience I enjoin the ministers to ask the pope for a cardinal of the holy Roman Church to be governor, protector and corrector of this fraternity, so that, always subjects at the feet of the same holy Church, steady in the Catholic faith, we may observe the poverty, the humility and the holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ which we firmly promised. Here ends the rule and life of the Lesser Brothers. The confirmation follows: let no one infringe this page of confirmation or oppose it by rash daring. Whoever presumes to try it, let him know he will incur the wrath of almighty God and of blessed Peter and Paul. Given at the Lateran, three days before the calends of December, in the eighth year of our pontificate. Honorius III.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] In nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti! [2] Haec est vita evangelii Jesu Christi, quam frater Franciscus petiit a domino papa concedi et confirmari sibi; et ille concessit et confirmavit sibi et suis fratribus habitis et futuris. [3] Frater Franciscus et quicumque erit caput istius religionis promittat obedientiam domino Innocentio papae et reverentiam et suis successoribus. [4] Et omnes alii fratres teneantur obedire fratri Francisco et eius successoribus.
passages.translation: In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is the life of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, which Brother Francis asked the lord pope to grant him and confirm; and he granted and confirmed it to him and to his brothers, present and to come. Brother Francis, and whoever will be head of this religion, is to promise obedience and reverence to the lord pope Innocent and his successors. And all the other brothers are bound to obey Brother Francis and his successors.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Regula et vita istorum fratrum haec est, scilicet vivere in obedientia, in castitate et sine proprio, et Domini nostri Jesu Christi doctrinam et vestigia sequi, qui dicit [2] «Si vis perfectus esse, vade (Mt 19,21) et vende omnia (cfr. Lc 18,22), quae habes, et da pauperibus et habebis thesaurum in caelo; et veni, sequere me» (Mt 19,21). [3] Et «Si quis vult post me venire, abneget semetipsum et tollat crucem suam et sequatur me» (Mt 16, 24). [4] Item «Si quis vult venire ad me et non odit patrem et matrem et uxorem et filios et fratres et sorores, adhuc autem et animam suam, non potest meus esse discipulus» (Lc 14,26). [5] Et «Omnis, qui reliquerit patrem aut matrem, fratres aut sorores, uxorem aut filios, domos aut agros propter me, centuplum accipiet et vitam aeternam possidebit» (cfr. Mt 19,29; Mc 10,29; Lc 18,29).
passages.translation: The rule and life of these brothers is this: to live in obedience, in chastity and without anything of one's own, and to follow the teaching and the footprints of our Lord Jesus Christ, who says: if you want to be perfect, go, sell all you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. And: if anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross and follow me. Again: if anyone wants to come to me and does not hate father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own soul, he cannot be my disciple. And: whoever has left father or mother, brothers or sisters, wife or children, houses or fields for my sake will receive a hundredfold and possess eternal life.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Si quis divina inspiratione volens accipere hanc vitam venerit ad nostros fratres, benigne recipiatur ab eis. [2] Quodsi fuerit firmus accipere vitam nostram, multum caveant sibi fratres, ne de suis temporalibus negotiis se intromittant, sed ad suum ministrum, quam citius possunt, eum repraesentent. [3] Minister vero benigne ipsum recipiat et confortet et vitae nostrae tenorem sibi diligenter exponat. [4] Quo facto, praedictus, si vult et potest spiritualiter sine impedimento, omnia sua vendat et ea omnia pauperibus studeat erogare. [5] Caveant sibi fratres et minister fratrum, quod de negotiis suis nullo modo intromittant se; [6] neque recipiant aliquam pecuniam neque per se neque per interpositam personam. [7] Si tamen indigent, alia necessaria corporis praeter pecuniam recipere possunt fratres causa necessitatis sicut alii pauperes. [8] Et cum reversus fuerit, minister concedat ei pannos probationis usque ad annum, scilicet duas tunicas sine caputio et cingulum et braccas et caparonem usque ad cingulum. [9] Finito vero anno et termino probationis recipiatur ad obedientiam. [10] Postea non licebit ei ad aliam religionem accedere neque «extra obedientiam evagari» iuxta mandatum domini papae et secundum evangelium; quia «nemo mittens manum ad aratrum et aspiciens retro aptus est regno Dei» (Lc 9,62). [11] Si autem aliquis venerit, qui sua dare non potest sine impedimento et habet spiritualem voluntatem, relinquat illa, et sufficit sibi. [12] Nullus recipiatur contra formam et institutionem sanctae Ecclesiae. [13] Alii vero fratres, qui promiserunt obedientiam, habeant unam tunicam cum caputio et aliam sine caputio, si necesse fuerit, et cingulum et braccas. [14] Et omnes fratres vilibus vestibus induantur, et possint eas repeciare de saccis et aliis peciis cum benedictione Dei; quia dicit Dominus in evangelio «Qui in veste pretiosa sunt et in deliciis» (Lc 7,25) et «qui mollibus vestiuntur, in domibus regum sunt» (Mt 11,8). [15] Et licet dicantur hypocritae, non tamen cessent bene facere nec quaerant caras vestes in hoc saeculo, ut possint habere vestimentum in regno caelorum.
passages.translation: If someone, wishing by divine inspiration to take this life, comes to our brothers, let them receive him kindly. If he is firm in taking our life, let the brothers carefully avoid meddling in his temporal business, and present him as soon as they can to their minister. Let the minister receive him kindly, encourage him, and set out carefully the tenor of our life. That done, if he wishes and spiritually can, without hindrance, let him sell all that is his and take care to give it to the poor. Let the brothers and the minister avoid meddling in his affairs in any way, and receive no money, by themselves or through another person. If they are in need, the brothers may receive, by necessity, the other things the body needs, except money, as other poor people do. When he has returned, let the minister give him the clothes of probation for up to a year: two tunics without a hood, the cord, trousers and a cape to the cord. When the year and the term of probation are over, let him be received into obedience. After that it will not be lawful for him to move to another religion or to wander outside obedience, according to the pope's command and the Gospel: no one who puts a hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God. If someone comes who cannot give what is his without hindrance, and has a spiritual will, let him leave those things, and that is enough for him. Let no one be received against the form and institution of the holy Church. The other brothers, who have promised obedience, are to have one tunic with a hood and another without, if needed, and the cord and trousers. Let all the brothers dress in poor clothes and they may patch them with sackcloth and other pieces, with God's blessing, because the Lord says in the Gospel that those who are in costly dress and in luxury, and those who dress softly, are in the houses of kings. And even if people call them hypocrites, let them not stop doing good, and let them not seek expensive clothes in this age, so that they may have clothing in the kingdom of heaven.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Dicit Dominus Hoc genus daemoniorum non potest exire nisi in ieiunio et oratione (cfr. Mc 9,28); [2] et iterum «Cum ieiunatis nolite fieri sicut hypocritae tristes» (Mt 6,16). [3] Propter hoc omnes fratres sive clerici sive laici faciant divinum officium, laudes et orationes, secundum quod debent facere. [4] Clerici faciant officium et dicant pro vivis et pro mortuis secundum consuetudinem clericorum. [5] Et pro defectu et negligentia fratrum dicant omni die Miserere mei Deus (Ps 50) cum Pater noster; [6] et pro fratribus defunctis dicant De profundis (Ps 129) cum Pater noster. [7] Et libros tantum necessarios ad implendum eorum officium possint habere. [8] Et laicis etiam scientibus legere psalterium liceat eis habere illud. [9] Aliis vero nescientibus litteras librum habere non liceat. [10] Laici dicant Credo in Deum et viginti quattuor Pater noster cum Gloria Patri pro matutino; pro laudibus vero quinque; pro prima Credo in Deum et septem Pater noster cum Gloria Patri; pro tertia, sexta et nona et unaquaque hora septem; pro vesperis duodecim; pro completorio Credo in Deum et septem Pater noster cum Gloria Patri; pro mortuis septem Pater noster cum Requiem aeternam; et pro defectu et negligentia fratrum tria Pater noster omni die. [11] Et similiter omnes fratres ieiunent a festo Omnium Sanctorum usque ad Natale et ab Epiphania, quando Dominus noster Jesus Christus incepit ieiunare usque ad Pascha. [12] Aliis autem temporibus non teneantur secundum hanc vitam nisi sexta feria ieiunare. [13] Et liceat eis manducare de omnibus cibis, qui apponuntur eis, secundum evangelium (cfr. Lc 10,8).
passages.translation: The Lord says: this kind of demon cannot come out except by fasting and prayer; and again: when you fast, do not become sad like the hypocrites. For this, let all the brothers, clerics or lay, do the divine office, the praises and the prayers, as they ought. Let the clerics do the office and pray for the living and the dead according to the custom of clerics. For the brothers' faults and negligences let them say the Miserere with the Our Father every day; and for the dead brothers the De profundis with the Our Father. They may have only the books needed to carry out their office. Lay brothers who know how to read the psalter may have it. The others, who do not know letters, may not have a book. Let the lay brothers say the Creed and twenty-four Our Fathers with the Glory for matins; five for lauds; for prime the Creed and seven Our Fathers with the Glory; for terce, sext and none, and for each of those hours, seven; twelve for vespers; for compline the Creed and seven Our Fathers with the Glory; for the dead, seven Our Fathers with the Requiem; and for the brothers' fault and negligence, three Our Fathers every day. Likewise let all the brothers fast from All Saints until Christmas, and from Epiphany, when our Lord Jesus Christ began to fast, until Easter. At other times, according to this life, they are bound to fast only on Friday. And they may eat any of the foods set before them, according to the Gospel.

passages.originalText: [1] In nomine Domini! [2] Omnes fratres, qui constituuntur ministri et servi aliorum fratrum, in provinciis et in locis, in quibus fuerint, collocent suos fratres, quos saepe visitent et spiritualiter moneant et confortent. [3] Et omnes alii fratres mei benedicti diligenter obediant eis in his, quae spectant ad salutem animae et non sunt contraria vitae nostrae. [4] Et faciant inter se sicut dicit Dominus «Quaecumque vultis, ut faciant vobis homines et vos facite illis» (Mt 7,12); [5] et «Quod non vis tibi fieri, non facias alteri». [6] Et recordentur ministri et servi, quod dicit Dominus Non veni ministrari, sed ministrare (Mt 20,28) et quia commissa est eis cura animarum fratrum, de quibus, si aliquid perderetur propter eorum culpam et malum exemplum, in die iudicii oportebit eos reddere rationem (cfr. Mt 12,36) coram Domino Jesu Christo.
passages.translation: In the name of the Lord. All the brothers who are appointed ministers and servants of the other brothers, in the provinces and places where they are, are to place their brothers, visit them often, and warn and encourage them spiritually. And all my other blessed brothers are to obey them carefully in what concerns the soul's salvation and is not contrary to our life. Let them do among themselves as the Lord says: whatever you want people to do to you, do that to them also; and: what you do not want done to you, do not do to another. And let the ministers and servants remember that the Lord says: I have not come to be served, but to serve; and that the care of the brothers' souls has been entrusted to them, for which, if anything were lost by their fault and bad example, they will have to give an account on the day of judgment before the Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Ideoque animas vestras et fratrum vestrorum custodite; quia horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis (Hebr 10,31). [2] Si quis autem ministrorum alicui fratrum aliquid contra vitam nostram praeciperet vel contra animam suam, non teneatur ei obedire; quia illa obedientia non est, in qua delictum vel peccatum committitur. [3] Verumtamen omnes fratres, qui sunt sub ministris et servis, facta ministrorum et servorum considerent rationabiliter et diligenter. [4] Et si viderint aliquem illorum carnaliter et non spiritualiter ambulare pro rectitudine vitae nostrae, post tertiam admonitionem, si non se emendaverit, in capitulo Pentecostes renuntient ministro et servo totius fraternitatis nulla contradictione impediente. [5] Si vero inter fratres ubicumque fuerit aliquis frater volens carnaliter et non spiritualiter ambulare, fratres, cum quibus est, moneant eum, instruant et corripiant humiliter et diligenter. [6] Quodsi ille post tertiam admonitionem noluerit se emendare, quam citius possunt, mittant eum vel significent suo ministro et servo, qui minister et servus de eo faciat, sicut sibi secundum Deum melius videbitur expedire. [7] Et caveant omnes fratres tam ministri et servi quam alii, quod propter peccatum alterius vel malum non turbentur vel irascantur, quia diabolus propter delictum unius multos vult corrumpere; [8] sed spiritualiter, sicut melius possunt, adiuvent illum qui peccavit, quia non est sanis opus medicus, sed male habentibus (cfr. Mt 9,12 cum Mc 2,17). [9] Similiter omnes fratres non habeant in hoc potestatem vel dominationem maxime inter se. [10] Sicut enim dicit Dominus in evangelio «Principes gentium dominantur eorum, et qui maiores sunt potestatem exercent in eos» (Mt 20,25), non sic erit inter fratres (cfr. Mt 20,26a). [11] Et quicumque voluerit inter eos maior fieri, sit eorum minister (cfr. Mt 20,26b) et servus. [12] Et qui maior est inter eos fiat sicut minor (cfr. Lc 22,26). [13] Nec aliquis frater malum faciat vel malum dicat alteri; [14] immo magis per caritatem spiritus voluntarie serviant et obediant invicem (cfr. Gal 5,13). [15] Et haec est vera et sancta obedientia Domini nostri Jesu Christi. [16] Et omnes fratres, quoties declinaverint a mandatis Domini et extra obedientiam evagaverint, sicut dicit propheta (Ps 118,21), sciant se esse maledictos extra obedientiam, quousque steterint in tali peccato scienter. [17] Et quando perseveraverint in mandatis Domini, quae promiserunt per sanctum evangelium et vitam ipsorum, sciant se in vera obedientia stare, et benedicti sint a Domino.
passages.translation: Guard your own souls and your brothers' souls, because it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. If one of the ministers commands a brother something against our life or against his soul, he is not bound to obey: that is not obedience in which a crime or a sin is committed. Yet all the brothers under the ministers and servants are to consider the ministers' and servants' actions reasonably and carefully. And if they see one of them walking according to the flesh and not the spirit, as regards the straightness of our life, after a third warning, if he has not corrected himself, let them report him at the Pentecost chapter to the minister and servant of the whole fraternity, with nothing allowed to block it. If anywhere among the brothers there is a brother who wants to walk according to the flesh and not the spirit, the brothers he is with are to warn, instruct and correct him humbly and carefully. If after a third warning he will not correct himself, let them as soon as they can send him or report him to his minister and servant, and let the minister and servant deal with him as seems best according to God. Let all the brothers, ministers and servants and the rest, beware of being disturbed or angry over another's sin or evil, because the devil wants to corrupt many through one person's offence; but spiritually, as best they can, let them help the one who has sinned, because it is not the healthy who need the physician, but those who are ill. Likewise let all the brothers not have power or domination in this, especially among themselves. As the Lord says in the Gospel, the rulers of the nations lord it over them and the great exercise power over them: it shall not be so among the brothers. And whoever wants to become the greater among them is to be their minister and servant. And whoever is greater among them is to become as the lesser. Let no brother do evil or speak evil to another; rather, through the charity of the Spirit, let them willingly serve and obey one another. And this is the true and holy obedience of our Lord Jesus Christ. All the brothers, whenever they have turned aside from the Lord's commands and gone outside obedience, are to know themselves cursed outside obedience, as long as they knowingly remain in that sin. And when they have persevered in the Lord's commands, which they promised by the holy Gospel and by their life, let them know they stand in true obedience, and let them be blessed by the Lord.

passages.originalText: [1] Fratres, in quibuscumque locis sunt, si non possunt vitam nostram observare, quam citius possunt, recurrant ad suum ministrum hoc sibi significantes. [2] Minister vero taliter eis studeat providere, sicut ipse vellet sibi fieri, si in consimili casu esset (cfr. Mt 7,12). [3] Et nullus vocetur prior, sed generaliter omnes vocentur fratres minores. [4] Et alter alterius lavet pedes (cfr. Joa 13,14).
passages.translation: The brothers, wherever they are, if they cannot observe our life, are to have recourse as soon as they can to their minister, letting him know. Let the minister take care to provide for them as he would want done for himself, were he in a like case. And let no one be called prior, but let everyone generally be called lesser brothers. And let one wash the other's feet.
passages.note: Medieval public-domain text, from the Latin Wikisource transcription (consulted on 11 Nov 2026). Editorial translation original to this app, not a critical edition.

passages.originalText: [1] Omnes fratres, in quibuscumque locis steterint apud alios ad serviendum vel laborandum, non sint camerarii neque cancellarii neque praesint in domibus, in quibus serviunt; nec recipiant aliquod officium, quod scandalum generet vel animae suae faciat detrimentum (cfr. Mc 8,36); [2] sed sint minores et subditi omnibus, qui in eadem domo sunt. [3] Et fratres, qui sciunt laborare, laborent et eandem artem exerceant, quam noverint, si non fuerit contra salutem animae et honeste poterit operari. [4] Nam propheta ait «Labores fructuum tuorum manducabis; beatus es et bene tibi erit» (Ps 127,2;-R); [5] et apostolus Qui non vult operari non manducet (cfr. 2 Thess 3,10); [6] et Unusquisque in ea arte et officio, in quo vocatus est, permaneat (cfr. 1 Cor 7,24). [7] Et pro labore possint recipere omnia necessaria praeter pecuniam. [8] Et cum necesse fuerit, vadant pro eleemosynis sicut alii pauperes. [9] Et liceat eis habere ferramenta et instrumenta suis artibus opportuna. [10] Omnes fratres studeant bonis operibus insudare, quia scriptum est Semper facito aliquid boni, ut te diabolus inveniat occupatum. [11] Et iterum Otiositas inimica est animae. [12] Ideo servi Dei semper orationi vel alicui bonae operationi insistere debent. [13] Caveant sibi fratres, ubicumque fuerint in eremis vel in aliis locis, quod nullum locum sibi approprient nec alicui defendant. [14] Et quicumque ad eos venerit amicus vel adversarius, fur vel latro benigne recipiatur. [15] Et ubicumque sunt fratres et in quocumque loco se invenerint, spiritualiter et diligenter debeant se revidere et honorare ad invicem sine murmuratione (1 Petr 4,9). [16] Et caveant sibi, quod non se ostendant tristes extrinsecus et nubilosos hypocritas; sed ostendant se gaudentes in Domino (cfr. Phil 4,4) et hilares et convenienter gratiosos.
passages.translation: All the brothers, wherever they stay with others to serve or to work, are not to be chamberlains or chancellors, nor to be in charge of the houses where they serve; nor are they to take any office that breeds scandal or harms their soul; but let them be lesser and subject to everyone in the same house. Brothers who know how to work are to work and practise the craft they know, if it is not against the soul's salvation and can be done honestly. For the prophet says: you will eat of the fruit of your labours; you are blessed, and it will be well with you; and the apostle: one who will not work, let him not eat; and: let each remain in the craft and office in which he was called. For their work they may receive everything needed, except money. And when it is necessary, let them go for alms like the other poor. They may have the tools and instruments suited to their crafts. Let all the brothers take pains to sweat at good works, because it is written: always be doing something good, so the devil finds you occupied. And again: idleness is the enemy of the soul. Therefore the servants of God must always press on in prayer or in some good work. Let the brothers, wherever they are, in hermitages or other places, beware of appropriating any place or of defending it against anyone. And whoever comes to them, friend or adversary, thief or robber, is to be received kindly. And wherever the brothers are, and in whatever place they find themselves, they ought spiritually and carefully to look to one another and honour one another, without murmuring. And let them beware of showing themselves outwardly sad and cloudy hypocrites; let them show themselves joyful in the Lord, cheerful and gracious as is fitting.
